```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(lme4)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
library(broom.mixed)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
# Sys.setenv(PROMPT_CONTROL_RESULTS = normalizePath(
#   "artifacts/phase1_results_combined_labeled_heuristic_v2.csv"
# ))

data_candidates <- c(
  Sys.getenv("PROMPT_CONTROL_RESULTS", unset = ""),
  "artifacts/phase1_results_combined_labeled_heuristic_v2.csv",
  "../artifacts/phase1_results_combined_labeled_heuristic_v2.csv"
)
data_candidates <- data_candidates[nzchar(data_candidates) & file.exists(data_candidates)]
if (length(data_candidates) == 0) {
  stop("Could not find phase1_results_combined_labeled.csv. Set PROMPT_CONTROL_RESULTS or run from the repository root.")
}
data_path <- data_candidates[[1]]
loader_candidates <- c("analysis/load_combined_results.R", "load_combined_results.R")
loader_candidates <- loader_candidates[file.exists(loader_candidates)]
if (!length(loader_candidates)) stop("Could not find load_combined_results.R.")
source(loader_candidates[[1]])
all_data <- load_combined_results(data_path)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}

model_levels <- c(
  "Llama-3.1-8B",
  "Llama-3.3-70B",
  "Qwen-2-7B",
  "Qwen-2.5-72B",
  "Gemma-4-12B",
  "Gemma-4-31B",
  "Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B",
  "Nemotron-3-Nano-4B",
  "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B",
  "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B",
  "GPT-6-Astra",
  "Claude-Opus-5.5",
  "Gemini-3.1-Pro"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Clean and derive useful variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------

score_cols <- c(
  "refusal_score",
  "compliance_score",
  "clarification_score",
  "abstention_score",
  "hierarchy_following_score",
  "unsafe_continuation_score",
  "stop_compliance_score"
)

score_cols <- intersect(score_cols, names(all_data))

family_levels <- c(
  "No-system-prompt",
  "Answer-first",
  "Clarify-first",
  "Evidence-first",
  "Hierarchy-first",
  "Minimal-safe-help",
  "Refuse-first",
  "Source-isolation-first",
  "Transform-classify-first"
)

family_short_levels <- c(
  "No Prompt",
  "Answer",
  "Clarify",
  "Evidence",
  "Hierarchy",
  "Safe Help",
  "Refuse",
  "Source",
  "Transform"
)

clarity_levels <- c(
  "none",
  "vague",
  "explicit",
  "explicit-fallback"
)

policy_levels <- c(
  "compliance",
  "refusal",
  "clarification",
  "hierarchy_preservation",
  "source_isolation",
  "safe_redirection"
)

df <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Clean model names
  # --------------------------------------------------------
  model_name_raw = na_if(str_trim(as.character(model_name)), ""),

  # Normalize punctuation so model IDs and display names match consistently.
  model_name_clean = str_remove_all(
    str_to_lower(model_name_raw), "[^a-z0-9]"
  ),

  model_name = case_when(
    # Recover the known legacy run; don't assign every missing name to Qwen.
    is.na(model_name_raw) & source_run == "phase1_qwen25_72b" ~
      "Qwen-2.5-72B",

    model_name_clean == "f2826a00ceef68f0f2b946d945ecc0477ce4450c" ~
      "Qwen-2-7B",

    # Identify distilled models before their underlying model families.
    str_detect(model_name_clean, "deepseek.*distill.*qwen.*32b") ~
      "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B",
    str_detect(model_name_clean, "deepseek.*distill.*llama.*70b") ~
      "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B",

    str_detect(model_name_clean, "llama318b") ~ "Llama-3.1-8B",
    str_detect(model_name_clean, "llama3370b") ~ "Llama-3.3-70B",
    str_detect(model_name_clean, "qwen2572b") ~ "Qwen-2.5-72B",
    str_detect(model_name_clean, "qwen27b") ~ "Qwen-2-7B",

    str_detect(model_name_clean, "gemma412b") ~ "Gemma-4-12B",
    str_detect(model_name_clean, "gemma431b") ~ "Gemma-4-31B",
    str_detect(model_name_clean, "qwen3635ba3b") ~ "Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B",
    str_detect(model_name_clean, "nemotron3nano4b") ~ "Nemotron-3-Nano-4B",

    str_detect(model_name_clean, "gpt6astra") ~ "GPT-6-Astra",
    str_detect(model_name_clean, "claudeopus55") ~ "Claude-Opus-5.5",
    str_detect(model_name_clean, "gemini31pro") ~ "Gemini-3.1-Pro",

    TRUE ~ model_name_raw
  ),

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Clean prompt family names
  # --------------------------------------------------------
  prompt_family = as.character(prompt_family),
  prompt_family = if_else(
    is.na(prompt_family) | prompt_family == "",
    "No-system-prompt",
    prompt_family
  ),
  prompt_family = str_replace_all(prompt_family, "_", "-"),
  prompt_family = str_replace_all(prompt_family, "\\s+", "-"),

  # Short prompt-family labels for plotting
  prompt_family_short = case_when(
    prompt_family == "No-system-prompt" ~ "No Prompt",
    prompt_family == "Answer-first" ~ "Answer",
    prompt_family == "Clarify-first" ~ "Clarify",
    prompt_family == "Evidence-first" ~ "Evidence",
    prompt_family == "Hierarchy-first" ~ "Hierarchy",
    prompt_family == "Minimal-safe-help" ~ "Safe Help",
    prompt_family == "Refuse-first" ~ "Refuse",
    prompt_family == "Source-isolation-first" ~ "Source",
    prompt_family == "Transform-classify-first" ~ "Transform",
    TRUE ~ prompt_family
  ),

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Clean clarity names
  # --------------------------------------------------------
  clarity_level = as.character(clarity_level),
  clarity_level = if_else(
    is.na(clarity_level) | clarity_level == "",
    "none",
    clarity_level
  ),
  clarity_level = str_replace_all(clarity_level, "_", "-"),
  clarity_level = str_to_lower(clarity_level),

  # --------------------------------------------------------
  # Clean clarity names (duplicate from original)
  # --------------------------------------------------------
  clarity_level = as.character(clarity_level),
  clarity_level = if_else(
    is.na(clarity_level) | clarity_level == "",
    "none",
    clarity_level
  ),
  clarity_level = str_replace_all(clarity_level, "_", "-"),
  clarity_level = str_to_lower(clarity_level),

  # Short display labels for plotting
  clarity_short = case_when(
    clarity_level == "none" ~ "None",
    clarity_level == "explicit" ~ "Explicit",
    clarity_level == "explicit-fallback" ~ "Fallback",
    clarity_level == "vague" ~ "Vague",
    TRUE ~ clarity_level
  ),

  # Safer than item_id if item_id changes across prompt variants
  item_key = factor(paste(benchmark, input_text, sep = " :: ")),

  item_safety = case_when(
    gold_label == "safe" ~ "safe",
    gold_label == "unsafe" ~ "unsafe",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ),

  malformed = !is.na(malformed_output)
) %>%
  mutate(
    prompt_family = factor(
      prompt_family,
      levels = union(family_levels, unique(prompt_family))
    ),

    prompt_family_short = factor(
      prompt_family_short,
      levels = union(family_short_levels, unique(prompt_family_short))
    ),

    clarity_level = factor(
      clarity_level,
      levels = c("none", "vague", "explicit", "explicit-fallback")
    ),

    clarity_short = factor(
      clarity_short,
      levels = c("None", "Vague", "Explicit", "Fallback")
    ),

    model_name = factor(
      model_name,
      levels = union(model_levels, unique(na.omit(model_name)))
    )
  )
    
  

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derive policy label if missing
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Best case: use policy_label from the LLM judge.
# Fallback: infer a rough policy from task-specific score columns.
# Use the fallback only for diagnostics, not the final paper labels.

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Clean raw LLM policy label
    # --------------------------------------------------------
    policy = as.character(llm_policy_label),
    policy = str_to_lower(str_trim(policy)),
    policy = str_replace_all(policy, "-", "_"),
    policy = str_replace_all(policy, "\\s+", "_"),

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Normalize possible variants into canonical policy labels
    # --------------------------------------------------------
    policy = case_when(
      policy %in% c("compliance", "comply", "answer", "acceptance") ~ "compliance",
      policy %in% c("refusal", "refuse") ~ "refusal",
      policy %in% c("clarification", "clarify") ~ "clarification",
      policy %in% c("hierarchy_preservation", "hierarchy_following", "hierarchy") ~ "hierarchy_preservation",
      policy %in% c("source_isolation", "source", "source_isolating") ~ "source_isolation",
      policy %in% c("safe_redirection", "safe_redirect", "minimal_safe_help", "safe_help") ~ "safe_redirection",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    policy = factor(policy, levels = policy_levels),

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Short display labels
    # --------------------------------------------------------
    policy_short = case_when(
      policy == "compliance" ~ "Compliance",
      policy == "refusal" ~ "Refusal",
      policy == "clarification" ~ "Clarification",
      policy == "hierarchy_preservation" ~ "Hierarchy",
      policy == "source_isolation" ~ "Source",
      policy == "safe_redirection" ~ "Safe Help",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    policy_short = factor(
      policy_short,
      levels = c(
        "Compliance",
        "Refusal",
        "Clarification",
        "Hierarchy",
        "Source",
        "Safe Help"
      )
    ),

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Make llm_policy_label match policy_short
    # --------------------------------------------------------
    llm_policy_label = policy_short
  )

# Quick design check
design_check <- df %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_models = n_distinct(model_name),
    n_prompt_families = n_distinct(prompt_family),
    n_clarity_levels = n_distinct(clarity_level),
    n_policy_labels_nonmissing = sum(!is.na(policy)),
    n_policy_labels_missing = sum(is.na(policy)),
    n_malformed = sum(malformed, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(design_check)

# ============================================================
# 2. Aggregate safety-boundary rates
# ============================================================

boundary_rates <- df %>%
  filter(item_safety %in% c("safe", "unsafe")) %>%
  group_by(model_name, benchmark, prompt_family, clarity_level) %>%
  summarise(
    harmful_compliance_rate = mean(compliance_score[item_safety == "unsafe"] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    unsafe_refusal_rate = mean(refusal_score[item_safety == "unsafe"] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),

    false_refusal_rate = mean(refusal_score[item_safety == "safe"] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    safe_compliance_rate = mean(compliance_score[item_safety == "safe"] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),

    n_safe = sum(item_safety == "safe"),
    n_unsafe = sum(item_safety == "unsafe"),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

boundary_rates
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 1: Safety boundary
# x = harmful compliance on unsafe items
# y = false refusal on safe items
# color = prompt family
# shape = model
# ============================================================

# --------------------------------------------------------
# Shared behavioral policy colors
# --------------------------------------------------------

policy_colors <- c(
  "Compliance"    = "#2EAF4A",  # green
  "Refusal"       = "#D64545",  # red
  "Clarification" = "#4D80FA",  # blue
  "Hierarchy"     = "#19ABB4",  # teal
  "Source"        = "#A85CF2",  # purple
  "Safe Help"     = "#F2A93B"   # orange
)

# Main analysis dataset
analysis_df <- df %>%
  filter(!malformed)

rate <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || all(is.na(x))) return(NA_real_)
  mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

boundary_df <- analysis_df %>%
  filter(item_safety %in% c("safe", "unsafe")) %>%
  group_by(model_name, prompt_family_short, clarity_level) %>%
  summarise(
    harmful_compliance_rate = rate(compliance_score[item_safety == "unsafe"] == 1),
    false_refusal_rate      = rate(refusal_score[item_safety == "safe"] == 1),
    safe_acceptance_rate    = rate(compliance_score[item_safety == "safe"] == 1),
    unsafe_refusal_rate     = rate(refusal_score[item_safety == "unsafe"] == 1),
    n_safe                  = sum(item_safety == "safe" & !is.na(refusal_score)),
    n_unsafe                = sum(item_safety == "unsafe" & !is.na(compliance_score)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

shape_vals <- setNames(
  rep(c(16, 17, 15, 18, 8, 3, 4, 7, 9, 10), length.out = nlevels(analysis_df$model_name)),
  levels(analysis_df$model_name)
)


frontier_df <- boundary_df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(harmful_compliance_rate),
    !is.na(false_refusal_rate)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    x = harmful_compliance_rate,
    y = false_refusal_rate
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Fit nonlinear exponential decay
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fit_exp_nls <- nls(
  y ~ c + a * exp(-b * x),
  data = frontier_df,
  start = list(
    c = 0.005,  # lower asymptote
    a = 0.20,   # initial height
    b = 8       # steepness
  ),
  control = nls.control(
    maxiter = 500,
    warnOnly = TRUE
  )
)

summary(fit_exp_nls)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Generate predictions for observed points
# ------------------------------------------------------------

frontier_df <- frontier_df %>%
  mutate(
    exp_pred = predict(fit_exp_nls, newdata = frontier_df)
  )

# R2 for fitted curve on original scale
exp_r2 <- cor(
  frontier_df$y,
  frontier_df$exp_pred,
  use = "complete.obs"
)^2

exp_r2

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Generate smooth curve for plotting
# ------------------------------------------------------------

curve_df <- tibble(
  x = seq(
    min(frontier_df$x, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(frontier_df$x, na.rm = TRUE),
    length.out = 300
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    pred_y = predict(fit_exp_nls, newdata = tibble(x = x))
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Plot safety boundary with fitted exponential curve
# ------------------------------------------------------------

p_boundary_family <- boundary_df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(harmful_compliance_rate),
    !is.na(false_refusal_rate)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = harmful_compliance_rate,
    y = false_refusal_rate,
    color = prompt_family_short,
    shape = model_name
  )) +

  # fitted nonlinear exponential curve
  geom_line(
    data = curve_df,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = pred_y
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 3
  ) +

  # model x prompt-family points
  geom_point(
    size = 5,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +

 scale_x_continuous(
  labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
  limits = c(0, .6),
  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))
) +
scale_y_continuous(
  labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
  limits = c(0, .6),
  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))
) +
coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +

  scale_shape_manual(values = shape_vals) +

  labs(
    x = "Harmful Compliance",
    y = "False Refusal",
    color = NULL,
    shape = NULL
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(
      colour = "black",
      linewidth = 2,
      linetype = "solid"
    ),
legend.position = c(0.72, 0.62),
  legend.justification = c("left", "center"),
  legend.box = "vertical",
  legend.background = element_rect(
    fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.80),
    color = NA
  ),
  legend.key = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA),
  legend.key.size = unit(0.8, "cm"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 30),
  legend.title = element_blank(),

    axis.text = element_text(size = 30),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 34),

    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 26,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    )
  ) +

  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(
        shape = 16,
        size = 7,
        alpha = 1,
        linewidth = 0
      )
    ),
    shape = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(
        color = "black",
        size = 5,
        alpha = 1
      )
    )
  )

policy_family_model_df <- analysis_df %>%

    !is.na(llm_policy_label),

    !is.na(prompt_family_short),

  ) %>%
  mutate(
    llm_policy_label = as.character(llm_policy_label),
    prompt_family_short = factor(
      prompt_family_short,
      levels = c(
        "Answer",
        "Refuse",
        "Clarify",
        "Evidence",
        "Hierarchy",
        "Safe Help",
        "Source",
        "Transform"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  count(model_name, prompt_family_short, llm_policy_label, name = "n") %>%
  complete(
    nesting(model_name, prompt_family_short),
    llm_policy_label,
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(model_name, prompt_family_short) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

# ============================================================
# PLOT 3: Aggregate effect of clarity on the safety boundary
# one point per clarity level
# ============================================================

library(grid)

clarity_boundary_df <- analysis_df %>%
  filter(item_safety %in% c("safe", "unsafe")) %>%
  group_by(clarity_short) %>%
  summarise(
    harmful_compliance_rate = mean(
      compliance_score[item_safety == "unsafe"] == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    false_refusal_rate = mean(
      refusal_score[item_safety == "safe"] == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    n_unsafe = sum(item_safety == "unsafe" & !is.na(compliance_score)),
    n_safe = sum(item_safety == "safe" & !is.na(refusal_score)),

    hc_se = sqrt(harmful_compliance_rate * (1 - harmful_compliance_rate) / n_unsafe),
    fr_se = sqrt(false_refusal_rate * (1 - false_refusal_rate) / n_safe),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hc_low = pmax(0, harmful_compliance_rate - 1.96 * hc_se),
    hc_high = pmin(1, harmful_compliance_rate + 1.96 * hc_se),

    fr_low = pmax(0, false_refusal_rate - 1.96 * fr_se),
    fr_high = pmin(1, false_refusal_rate + 1.96 * fr_se)
  )

clarity_boundary_df

# ============================================================
# Individual condition points:
# each grey point = model x prompt family x clarity level
# ============================================================

clarity_boundary_individual_df <- analysis_df %>%
  filter(item_safety %in% c("safe", "unsafe")) %>%
  group_by(model_name, prompt_family, clarity_short) %>%
  summarise(
    harmful_compliance_rate = mean(
      compliance_score[item_safety == "unsafe"] == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    false_refusal_rate = mean(
      refusal_score[item_safety == "safe"] == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    n_unsafe = sum(item_safety == "unsafe" & !is.na(compliance_score)),
    n_safe = sum(item_safety == "safe" & !is.na(refusal_score)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(harmful_compliance_rate),
    !is.na(false_refusal_rate),
    n_unsafe > 0,
    n_safe > 0
  )

x_max <- max(
  c(
    clarity_boundary_individual_df$harmful_compliance_rate,
    clarity_boundary_df$hc_high
  ),
  na.rm = TRUE

# ============================================================
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Load and clean

df <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    prompt_family = if_else(
      is.na(prompt_family) | prompt_family == "",
      "No-system-prompt",
      prompt_family
    ),
    clarity_level = if_else(
      is.na(clarity_level) | clarity_level == "",
      "none",
      clarity_level
    ),

    model_name = case_when(
      model_name == "f2826a00ceef68f0f2b946d945ecc0477ce4450c" ~ "Qwen2-7B",
      TRUE ~ as.character(model_name)
    ),

    item_key = paste(benchmark, item_id, input_text, sep = " :: "),

    item_safety = case_when(
      gold_label == "safe" ~ "safe",
      gold_label == "unsafe" ~ "unsafe",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    malformed = !is.na(malformed_output),

    policy = case_when(
      !is.na(policy_label) ~ as.character(policy_label),
      refusal_score == 1 ~ "Refusal",
      compliance_score == 1 ~ "Compliance",
      clarification_score == 1 ~ "Clarification",
      hierarchy_following_score == 1 ~ "Hierarchy preservation",
      stop_compliance_score == 1 ~ "Source isolation",
      abstention_score == 1 ~ "Abstention",
      unsafe_continuation_score == 1 ~ "Unsafe continuation",
      TRUE ~ "Unclassified"
    ),

    prompt_family = factor(prompt_family),
    clarity_level = factor(
      clarity_level,
      levels = c("none", "vague", "explicit", "explicit_fallback")
    ),
    model_name = factor(model_name),
    benchmark = factor(benchmark),
    item_safety = factor(item_safety, levels = c("safe", "unsafe")),
    policy = factor(policy)
  ) %>%
  filter(!malformed)

df %>%
  summarise(

    n_clarity = n_distinct(clarity_level),
    n_policies = n_distinct(policy)
  )

df %>%
  count(model_name, prompt_family, clarity_level, benchmark)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# 1A. Does prompt family change classified policy?
# Includes:
#   1. Omnibus chi-square
#   2. Standardized residuals
#   3. Planned routing tests
#   4. Largest unexpected cells
#   5. Item-level switch rate from No Prompt baseline
#   6. Compact summary table
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Create robust analysis labels
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# This makes the code work whether you are using prompt_family
# or the original prompt_family column.

policy_analysis_df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    analysis_family = case_when(
      "prompt_family" %in% names(.) ~ as.character(prompt_family),
      TRUE ~ as.character(prompt_family)
    ),

    analysis_family = case_when(
      analysis_family %in% c("No-system-prompt", "No_system_prompt", "none", "No prompt") ~ "No Prompt",
      analysis_family %in% c("Answer-first", "Answer_first") ~ "Answer",
      analysis_family %in% c("Clarify-first", "Clarify_first") ~ "Clarify",
      analysis_family %in% c("Evidence-first", "Evidence_first") ~ "Evidence",
      analysis_family %in% c("Hierarchy-first", "Hierarchy_first") ~ "Hierarchy",
      analysis_family %in% c("Minimal-safe-help", "Minimal_safe_help") ~ "Safe Help",
      analysis_family %in% c("Refuse-first", "Refuse_first") ~ "Refuse",
      analysis_family %in% c("Source-isolation-first", "Source_isolation_first") ~ "Source",
      analysis_family %in% c("Transform-classify-first", "Transform_classify_first") ~ "Transform",
      TRUE ~ analysis_family
    ),

    analysis_policy = case_when(
      "llm_policy_label" %in% names(.) ~ as.character(llm_policy_label),
      "policy" %in% names(.) ~ as.character(policy),
      TRUE ~ as.character(policy)
    ),

    analysis_policy = case_when(
      analysis_policy %in% c("compliance", "Compliance") ~ "Compliance",
      analysis_policy %in% c("refusal", "Refusal") ~ "Refusal",
      analysis_policy %in% c("clarification", "Clarification") ~ "Clarification",
      analysis_policy %in% c("hierarchy_preservation", "Hierarchy preservation", "Hierarchy") ~ "Hierarchy",
      analysis_policy %in% c("source_isolation", "Source isolation", "Source") ~ "Source",
      analysis_policy %in% c("safe_redirection", "Safe Redirection", "Safe Help") ~ "Safe Help",
      TRUE ~ analysis_policy
    ),

    analysis_family = factor(
      analysis_family,
      levels = c(
        "No Prompt",
        "Answer",
        "Clarify",
        "Evidence",
        "Hierarchy",
        "Safe Help",
        "Refuse",
        "Source",
        "Transform"
      )
    ),

    analysis_policy = factor(
      analysis_policy,
      levels = c(
        "Compliance",
        "Refusal",
        "Clarification",
        "Hierarchy",
        "Source",
        "Safe Help"
      )
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Omnibus chi-square: prompt family x output policy
# ------------------------------------------------------------

policy_family_df <- policy_analysis_df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(analysis_family),
    !is.na(analysis_policy)
  )

policy_family_tab <- policy_family_df %>%
  count(analysis_family, analysis_policy, name = "n") %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    analysis_family,
    analysis_policy,
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  xtabs(n ~ analysis_family + analysis_policy, data = .)

chisq_family_policy <- chisq.test(policy_family_tab)

chisq_family_policy
effectsize::cramers_v(policy_family_tab)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Standardized residuals and cell-level effect description
# ------------------------------------------------------------
observed_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(policy_family_tab)) %>%
  rename(
    prompt_family = analysis_family,
    policy = analysis_policy,
    observed = Freq
  )

expected_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(chisq_family_policy$expected)) %>%
  rename(
    prompt_family = analysis_family,
    policy = analysis_policy,
    expected = Freq
  )

resid_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(chisq_family_policy$stdres)) %>%
  rename(
    prompt_family = analysis_family,
    policy = analysis_policy,
    std_resid = Freq
  )

family_policy_residuals <- observed_df %>%
  left_join(expected_df, by = c("prompt_family", "policy")) %>%
  left_join(resid_df, by = c("prompt_family", "policy")) %>%
  group_by(prompt_family) %>%
  mutate(
    family_total = sum(observed),
    observed_prop = observed / family_total,
    expected_prop = expected / family_total,
    pp_diff = observed_prop - expected_prop,
    lift = observed / expected
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    cell_p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(std_resid)),
    cell_p_bh = p.adjust(cell_p, method = "BH"),
    chi_contribution = (observed - expected)^2 / expected
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(std_resid)))

family_policy_residuals %>%
  select(
    prompt_family,
    policy,
    observed,
    expected,
    observed_prop,
    expected_prop,
    pp_diff,
    lift,
    std_resid,
    cell_p_bh,
    chi_contribution
  ) %>%
  print(n = 40)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Planned routing tests
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# These test whether each prompt family increases its predicted policy
# relative to all other prompt families.

planned_cells <- tribble(
  ~prompt_family, ~target_policy,
  "Answer",       "Compliance",
  "Clarify",      "Clarification",
  "Refuse",       "Refusal",
  "Hierarchy",    "Hierarchy",
  "Source",       "Source",
  "Safe Help",    "Safe Help"
)

run_planned_cell_test <- function(dat, fam, pol) {

  d <- dat %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(analysis_family),
      !is.na(analysis_policy),
      analysis_family != "No Prompt"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      is_family = analysis_family == fam,
      is_policy = analysis_policy == pol
    )

  tab <- matrix(
    c(
      sum(!d$is_family & !d$is_policy, na.rm = TRUE),
      sum(!d$is_family &  d$is_policy, na.rm = TRUE),
      sum( d$is_family & !d$is_policy, na.rm = TRUE),
      sum( d$is_family &  d$is_policy, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    nrow = 2,
    byrow = TRUE,
    dimnames = list(
      family = c("Other families", fam),
      policy = c("Other policies", pol)
    )
  )

  test <- chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE)

  a <- tab[2, 2]  # target family + target policy
  b <- tab[2, 1]  # target family + other policies
  c <- tab[1, 2]  # other families + target policy
  d0 <- tab[1, 1] # other families + other policies

  odds_ratio <- ((a + 0.5) * (d0 + 0.5)) / ((b + 0.5) * (c + 0.5))

  prop_in_family <- a / (a + b)
  prop_other_families <- c / (c + d0)

  tibble(
    prompt_family = fam,
    target_policy = pol,
    n_family = a + b,
    n_other_families = c + d0,
    target_n_in_family = a,
    target_n_other_families = c,
    prop_in_family = prop_in_family,
    prop_other_families = prop_other_families,
    pp_diff = prop_in_family - prop_other_families,
    odds_ratio = odds_ratio,
    chi_square = unname(test$statistic),
    df = unname(test$parameter),
    p = test$p.value
  )
}

planned_routing_tests <- planned_cells %>%
  pmap_dfr(~ run_planned_cell_test(policy_analysis_df, ..1, ..2)) %>%
  mutate(
    p_bh = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(pp_diff)))

planned_routing_tests

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Join planned tests with omnibus residuals
# ------------------------------------------------------------

planned_routing_with_residuals <- planned_routing_tests %>%
  left_join(
    family_policy_residuals %>%
      select(
        prompt_family,
        policy,
        observed,
        expected,
        observed_prop,
        expected_prop,
        std_resid,
        lift,
        chi_contribution
      ),
    by = c(
      "prompt_family" = "prompt_family",
      "target_policy" = "policy"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(std_resid)))

planned_routing_with_residuals

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Largest unexpected cells
# ------------------------------------------------------------

unexpected_cells <- family_policy_residuals %>%
  anti_join(
    planned_cells,
    by = c(
      "prompt_family" = "prompt_family",
      "policy" = "target_policy"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    direction = if_else(
      std_resid > 0,
      "More than expected",
      "Less than expected"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(std_resid)))

unexpected_cells %>%
  select(
    prompt_family,
    policy,
    direction,
    observed,
    expected,
    observed_prop,
    expected_prop,
    pp_diff,
    lift,
    std_resid,
    cell_p_bh,
    chi_contribution
  ) %>%
  print(n = 30)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Item-level change from No Prompt baseline
# ------------------------------------------------------------

baseline_df <- policy_analysis_df %>%
  filter(
    analysis_family == "No Prompt" |
      prompt_family == "No-system-prompt" |
      clarity_level == "none"
  ) %>%
  group_by(model_name, benchmark, item_key) %>%
  summarise(
    baseline_policy = first(as.character(analysis_policy)),
    n_baseline_rows = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Quick check: should usually be one baseline row per model x benchmark x item
baseline_check <- baseline_df %>%
  count(n_baseline_rows, sort = TRUE)

baseline_check

item_change_df <- policy_analysis_df %>%
  filter(
    !(analysis_family == "No Prompt" |
        prompt_family == "No-system-prompt" |
        clarity_level == "none")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    current_policy = as.character(analysis_policy)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    baseline_df,
    by = c("model_name", "benchmark", "item_key")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    policy_changed = current_policy != baseline_policy
  )

missing_baseline_check <- item_change_df %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_missing_baseline = sum(is.na(baseline_policy)),
    pct_missing_baseline = mean(is.na(baseline_policy)) * 100
  )

missing_baseline_check

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Switch rate by prompt family
# ------------------------------------------------------------

prompt_family_switch_rate <- item_change_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(baseline_policy), !is.na(current_policy)) %>%
  group_by(analysis_family) %>%
  summarise(
    n_prompt_item_rows = n(),

    pct_changed_from_baseline = mean(policy_changed, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rename(prompt_family = analysis_family) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_changed_from_baseline))

prompt_family_switch_rate

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Aggregate switch rate across all non-baseline prompts
# ------------------------------------------------------------

aggregate_switch_rate <- item_change_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(baseline_policy), !is.na(current_policy)) %>%
  summarise(
    n_prompt_item_rows = n(),
    n_changed = sum(policy_changed, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_changed_from_baseline = mean(policy_changed, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )

aggregate_switch_rate

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Policy transition table from baseline to prompt condition
# ------------------------------------------------------------

policy_transition_by_family <- item_change_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(baseline_policy), !is.na(current_policy)) %>%
  count(
    analysis_family,
    baseline_policy,
    current_policy,

  ) %>%
  group_by(analysis_family, baseline_policy) %>%

policy_transition_by_family

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Compact table for writing the paper
# ------------------------------------------------------------

prompt_family_summary_table <- planned_routing_with_residuals %>%
  left_join(
    prompt_family_switch_rate,

  ) %>%
  transmute(
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# clarity on the frontier tradeoff:

# ============================================================
# Prompt clarity and frontier position
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(effectsize)
library(emmeans)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Build frontier-position dataframe
# ------------------------------------------------------------

clarity_frontier_df <- boundary_df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(harmful_compliance_rate),
    !is.na(false_refusal_rate)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    clarity_level = as.character(clarity_level),
    clarity_level = str_replace_all(clarity_level, "_", "-"),
    clarity_level = factor(
      clarity_level,
      levels = c("none", "vague", "explicit", "explicit-fallback")
    ),

    clarity_short = case_when(
      clarity_level == "none" ~ "None",
      clarity_level == "vague" ~ "Vague",
      clarity_level == "explicit" ~ "Explicit",
      clarity_level == "explicit-fallback" ~ "Fallback",
      TRUE ~ as.character(clarity_level)
    ),
    clarity_short = factor(
      clarity_short,
      levels = c("None", "Vague", "Explicit", "Fallback")
    ),

    harmful_compliance_z = as.numeric(scale(harmful_compliance_rate)),
    false_refusal_z = as.numeric(scale(false_refusal_rate)),

    # Higher = more compliance-biased:
    # higher harmful compliance and lower false refusal.
    frontier_position = harmful_compliance_z - false_refusal_z,

    # Lower = closer to ideal point.
    boundary_error_distance = sqrt(
      harmful_compliance_rate^2 + false_refusal_rate^2
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Aggregate clarity effect, including No Prompt / None
# This matches Figure 4.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

clarity_frontier_lm_all <- lm(
  frontier_position ~ clarity_short + model_name,
  data = clarity_frontier_df
)

summary(clarity_frontier_lm_all)
anova(clarity_frontier_lm_all)
effectsize::eta_squared(clarity_frontier_lm_all, partial = TRUE)

emmeans(clarity_frontier_lm_all, ~ clarity_short)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
    df$harmful_compliance_rate <= df$harmful_compliance_rate[i] &
      df$false_refusal_rate <= df$false_refusal_rate[i] &
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# Do output policies predict position on the refusal-compliance frontier?
# ============================================================
# ============================================================
# Bridge analysis:
# Do output policies predict position on the refusal-compliance frontier?
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Helper functions for consistent keys
# ------------------------------------------------------------

clean_model_name <- function(x) {
  x_raw <- as.character(x)
  x_clean <- str_to_lower(x_raw)

  case_when(
    is.na(x_raw) ~ "Qwen-2.5-72B",

    x_raw == "f2826a00ceef68f0f2b946d945ecc0477ce4450c" ~ "Qwen-2-7B",

    str_detect(x_clean, "llama[-_\\.]*3\\.1[-_\\.]*8b") ~ "Llama-3.1-8B",
    str_detect(x_clean, "llama[-_\\.]*3\\.3[-_\\.]*70b") ~ "Llama-3.3-70B",

    str_detect(x_clean, "qwen[-_\\.]*2[-_\\.]*5[-_\\.]*72b") ~ "Qwen-2.5-72B",
    str_detect(x_clean, "qwen[-_\\.]*2[-_\\.]*7b|qwen2[-_\\.]*7b") ~ "Qwen-2-7B",

    TRUE ~ x_raw
  )
}

clean_family <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)

  case_when(
    x %in% c("No-system-prompt", "No_system_prompt", "No Prompt", "none") ~ "No Prompt",
    x %in% c("Answer-first", "Answer_first", "Answer") ~ "Answer",
    x %in% c("Clarify-first", "Clarify_first", "Clarify") ~ "Clarify",
    x %in% c("Evidence-first", "Evidence_first", "Evidence") ~ "Evidence",
    x %in% c("Hierarchy-first", "Hierarchy_first", "Hierarchy") ~ "Hierarchy",
    x %in% c("Minimal-safe-help", "Minimal_safe_help", "Safe Help") ~ "Safe Help",
    x %in% c("Refuse-first", "Refuse_first", "Refuse") ~ "Refuse",
    x %in% c("Source-isolation-first", "Source_isolation_first", "Source") ~ "Source",
    x %in% c("Transform-classify-first", "Transform_classify_first", "Transform") ~ "Transform",
    TRUE ~ x
  )
}

clean_clarity <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    as.character() %>%
    str_replace_all("_", "-") %>%
    str_to_lower()
}

clean_policy <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- str_to_lower(str_trim(x))
  x <- str_replace_all(x, "-", "_")
  x <- str_replace_all(x, "\\s+", "_")

  case_when(
    x %in% c("compliance", "answer") ~ "compliance",
    x %in% c("refusal", "refuse") ~ "refusal",
    x %in% c("clarification", "clarify") ~ "clarification",
    x %in% c("hierarchy", "hierarchy_preservation") ~ "hierarchy_preservation",
    x %in% c("source", "source_isolation") ~ "source_isolation",
    x %in% c("safe_help", "safe_redirection") ~ "safe_redirection",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Standardize frontier-condition dataframe
# ------------------------------------------------------------

frontier_condition_df_clean <- frontier_condition_df %>%
  mutate(
    model_name = clean_model_name(model_name),
    prompt_family_short = clean_family(prompt_family_short),
    clarity_level = clean_clarity(clarity_level)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build policy composition using matching keys
# ------------------------------------------------------------

policy_condition_df_clean <- df %>%
  mutate(
    model_name = clean_model_name(model_name),

    prompt_family_for_key = if ("prompt_family_short" %in% names(.)) {
      as.character(prompt_family_short)
    } else {
      as.character(prompt_family)
    },

    prompt_family_short = clean_family(prompt_family_for_key),
    clarity_level = clean_clarity(clarity_level),

    policy_for_pivot = if ("policy" %in% names(.)) {
      clean_policy(policy)
    } else {
      clean_policy(llm_policy_label)
    }
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(policy_for_pivot)) %>%
  count(
    model_name,
    prompt_family_short,
    clarity_level,
    policy_for_pivot,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%
  group_by(model_name, prompt_family_short, clarity_level) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(
    model_name,
    prompt_family_short,
    clarity_level,
    policy_for_pivot,
    prop
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = policy_for_pivot,
    values_from = prop,
    values_fill = 0,
    names_prefix = "policy_"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Add any missing policy columns as zeros
# ------------------------------------------------------------

needed_policy_cols <- c(
  "policy_compliance",
  "policy_refusal",
  "policy_clarification",
  "policy_hierarchy_preservation",
  "policy_source_isolation",
  "policy_safe_redirection"
)

for (col in needed_policy_cols) {
  if (!col %in% names(policy_condition_df_clean)) {
    policy_condition_df_clean[[col]] <- 0
  }
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Diagnose key matching
# ------------------------------------------------------------

frontier_keys <- frontier_condition_df_clean %>%
  distinct(model_name, prompt_family_short, clarity_level)

policy_keys <- policy_condition_df_clean %>%
  distinct(model_name, prompt_family_short, clarity_level)

missing_from_policy <- frontier_keys %>%
  anti_join(
    policy_keys,
    by = c("model_name", "prompt_family_short", "clarity_level")
  )

missing_from_frontier <- policy_keys %>%
  anti_join(
    frontier_keys,
    by = c("model_name", "prompt_family_short", "clarity_level")
  )

missing_from_policy
missing_from_frontier

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Join policy composition to frontier position
# ------------------------------------------------------------

policy_frontier_df <- frontier_condition_df_clean %>%
  left_join(
    policy_condition_df_clean,
    by = c("model_name", "prompt_family_short", "clarity_level")
  )

policy_frontier_df %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_missing_compliance = sum(is.na(policy_compliance)),
    n_missing_refusal = sum(is.na(policy_refusal)),
    pct_missing_compliance = mean(is.na(policy_compliance)) * 100,
    pct_missing_refusal = mean(is.na(policy_refusal)) * 100
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Correlations between policy composition and frontier position
# ------------------------------------------------------------

safe_cor <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- complete.cases(x, y)
  if (sum(ok) < 3) return(NA_real_)
  cor(x[ok], y[ok])
}

policy_frontier_correlations <- policy_frontier_df %>%
  select(frontier_position, all_of(needed_policy_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(needed_policy_cols),
    names_to = "policy",
    values_to = "policy_rate"
  ) %>%
  group_by(policy) %>%
  summarise(
    n_complete = sum(complete.cases(policy_rate, frontier_position)),
    r = safe_cor(policy_rate, frontier_position),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(r)))

policy_frontier_correlations

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Regression: policy composition predicting frontier position
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Drop safe_redirection as the reference because policy proportions sum to 1.

policy_frontier_model_df <- policy_frontier_df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(frontier_position),
    if_all(all_of(needed_policy_cols), ~ !is.na(.x))
  )

frontier_policy_lm <- lm(
  frontier_position ~
    policy_compliance +
    policy_refusal +
    policy_clarification +
    policy_hierarchy_preservation +
    policy_source_isolation +
    model_name,
  data = policy_frontier_model_df
)

summary(frontier_policy_lm)
anova(frontier_policy_lm)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Compare policy-composition model against model-only baseline
# ------------------------------------------------------------

frontier_model_only <- lm(
  frontier_position ~ model_name,
  data = policy_frontier_model_df
)

anova(frontier_model_only, frontier_policy_lm)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# SIGNAL DETECTION ANALYSIS
#
# Signal         = unsafe request
# Positive call  = refusal
#
# Hit            = refuse unsafe request
# False alarm    = refuse safe request
#
# d'             = sensitivity / discrimination
# criterion (c)  = response bias
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
library(scales)
library(grid)


# ============================================================
# 1. CONDITION-LEVEL SDT MEASURES
# One observation = model x prompt family x clarity
# ============================================================

sdt_df <- analysis_df %>%
  filter(
    item_safety %in% c("safe", "unsafe"),
    !is.na(refusal_score)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    signal  = item_safety == "unsafe",
    refused = refusal_score == 1
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    model_name,
    prompt_family_short,
    clarity_level
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    hits               = sum(signal & refused),
    misses             = sum(signal & !refused),
    false_alarms       = sum(!signal & refused),
    correct_rejections = sum(!signal & !refused),

    n_signal = hits + misses,
    n_noise  = false_alarms + correct_rejections,

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Hautus/loglinear correction:
    # prevents infinite z values when rates are exactly 0 or 1
    hit_rate =
      (hits + 0.5) / (n_signal + 1),

    false_alarm_rate =
      (false_alarms + 0.5) / (n_noise + 1),

    z_hit = qnorm(hit_rate),
    z_fa  = qnorm(false_alarm_rate),

    # Sensitivity
    d_prime = z_hit - z_fa,

    # Criterion
    # Positive = more conservative / less willing to refuse
    # Negative = more liberal / more willing to refuse
    criterion = -0.5 * (z_hit + z_fa),

    # AUC implied by equal-variance SDT
    auc = pnorm(d_prime / sqrt(2))
  )


# ============================================================
# 2. SIMPLE INFERENTIAL TESTS
#
# Baseline has no meaningful clarity level, so use the
# fully crossed prompted conditions for prompt/clarity tests.
# ============================================================

sdt_prompted <- sdt_df %>%
  filter(
    prompt_family_short != "No Prompt",
    !is.na(clarity_level),
    clarity_level != "none"
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Sensitivity model
#
# Question:
# Do model, prompt family, or clarity change discriminability?
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_dprime <- lm(
  d_prime ~
    model_name +
    prompt_family_short +
    clarity_level,
  data = sdt_prompted
)

dprime_anova <- car::Anova(
  m_dprime,
  type = 2
)

dprime_anova


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Criterion model
#
# Question:
# Do model, prompt family, or clarity shift response bias?
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_criterion <- lm(
  criterion ~
    model_name +
    prompt_family_short +
    clarity_level,
  data = sdt_prompted
)

criterion_anova <- car::Anova(
  m_criterion,
  type = 2
)

criterion_anova


# ============================================================
# 3. MAKE REPORTABLE STATISTICS TABLE
# Includes partial eta-squared
# ============================================================

extract_anova_stats <- function(model, outcome_name) {

  a <- car::Anova(model, type = 2) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    rownames_to_column("effect")

  df_error <- df.residual(model)

  a %>%
    filter(effect != "Residuals") %>%
    transmute(
      outcome = outcome_name,
      effect,
      df1 = Df,
      df2 = df_error,
      F = `F value`,
      p = `Pr(>F)`,
      partial_eta2 =
        (F * df1) /
        ((F * df1) + df2)
    )
}

sdt_stats <- bind_rows(
  extract_anova_stats(
    m_dprime,
    "d_prime"
  ),
  extract_anova_stats(
    m_criterion,
    "criterion"
  )
)

sdt_stats


# Nicely formatted version for inspecting/reporting
sdt_stats_report <- sdt_stats %>%
  mutate(
    F = round(F, 2),
    p_report = case_when(
      p < .001 ~ "< .001",
      TRUE ~ sprintf("= %.3f", p)
    ),
    partial_eta2 = round(partial_eta2, 2)
  )

sdt_stats_report


# ============================================================
# 4. MODEL DESCRIPTIVES
# Useful for reporting direction of model effects
# ============================================================

model_sdt_summary <- sdt_prompted %>%
  group_by(model_name) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_d_prime = mean(d_prime),
    se_d_prime =
      sd(d_prime) / sqrt(n()),

    mean_criterion = mean(criterion),
    se_criterion =
      sd(criterion) / sqrt(n()),

    mean_auc = mean(auc),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

model_sdt_summary


# ============================================================
# 5. PAIRWISE MODEL COMPARISONS
#
# Use these if the omnibus model effect on d' or criterion
# is significant.
# ============================================================

dprime_model_pairs <- emmeans(
  m_dprime,
  pairwise ~ model_name,
  adjust = "tukey"
)

criterion_model_pairs <- emmeans(
  m_criterion,
  pairwise ~ model_name,
  adjust = "tukey"
)

dprime_model_pairs
criterion_model_pairs


# ============================================================
# 6. COLLAPSE ACROSS CLARITY FOR THE TWO MAIN ROC FIGURES
#
# One point = model x prompt family
#
# We recompute from raw counts rather than averaging rates.
# ============================================================

prompt_roc <- analysis_df %>%
  filter(
    item_safety %in% c("safe", "unsafe"),
    !is.na(refusal_score)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    signal  = item_safety == "unsafe",
    refused = refusal_score == 1
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    model_name,
    prompt_family_short
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    hits               = sum(signal & refused),
    misses             = sum(signal & !refused),
    false_alarms       = sum(!signal & refused),
    correct_rejections = sum(!signal & !refused),

    n_signal = hits + misses,
    n_noise  = false_alarms + correct_rejections,

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hit_rate =
      (hits + 0.5) / (n_signal + 1),

    false_alarm_rate =
      (false_alarms + 0.5) / (n_noise + 1),

    d_prime =
      qnorm(hit_rate) -
      qnorm(false_alarm_rate)
  )


# ============================================================
# 7. SIMPLE EQUAL-VARIANCE SDT FIT FOR EACH MODEL
#
# Under equal-variance SDT:
#
#   z(H) = z(FA) + d'
#
# Therefore each model needs only ONE fitted parameter: d'.
#
# This guarantees a proper monotonic ROC.
# ============================================================

model_sdt_fits <- prompt_roc %>%
  group_by(model_name) %>%
  summarise(
    d_prime_fit = mean(d_prime),
    auc_fit = pnorm(d_prime_fit / sqrt(2)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

model_sdt_fits


# Generate the fitted ROC curves
roc_curves <- model_sdt_fits %>%
  tidyr::crossing(
    false_alarm_rate =
      seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 500)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hit_rate =
      pnorm(
        qnorm(false_alarm_rate) +
          d_prime_fit
      )
  )


# ============================================================
# 8. PAPER THEME
# Based on your existing figure style
# ============================================================

paper_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),

    text = element_text(

    ),

    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

      linetype = "solid"
    ),

    legend.key.size = unit(
      1.5,
      "cm"
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 24
    )
  )


# ============================================================

p_roc_prompts <- ggplot(
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# SDT ROC FIGURE — ONE PANEL PER MODEL
#
# Color = prompt family
# Black curve = fitted SDT ROC
# Panel title = model name + fitted d'
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(grid)


# ============================================================
# 1. COMPUTE OBSERVED OPERATING POINTS
# Collapse across clarity
# ============================================================

prompt_roc <- analysis_df %>%
  filter(
    item_safety %in% c("safe", "unsafe"),
    !is.na(refusal_score)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    signal = item_safety == "unsafe",
    refused = refusal_score == 1
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    model_name,
    prompt_family_short
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    hits = sum(signal & refused),
    misses = sum(signal & !refused),

    false_alarms = sum(!signal & refused),
    correct_rejections = sum(!signal & !refused),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    n_signal = hits + misses,
    n_noise = false_alarms + correct_rejections
  ) %>%
  filter(n_signal > 0, n_noise > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    # Loglinear correction
    hit_rate = (hits + 0.5) / (n_signal + 1),

    false_alarm_rate =
      (false_alarms + 0.5) / (n_noise + 1),

    # Signal detection sensitivity
    d_prime =
      qnorm(hit_rate) -
      qnorm(false_alarm_rate)
  )


# ============================================================
# 2. FIT ONE SDT ROC PER MODEL
#
# Equal-variance Gaussian SDT:
# z(H) = z(FA) + d'
#
# Estimate each model's d' from its prompt operating points.
# ============================================================

model_sdt_fits <- prompt_roc %>%
  group_by(model_name) %>%
  summarise(
    d_prime_fit = mean(d_prime),
    auc_fit = pnorm(d_prime_fit / sqrt(2)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Display estimates
print(model_sdt_fits)


# ============================================================
# 3. GENERATE FITTED ROC CURVES
# ============================================================

roc_curves <- model_sdt_fits %>%
  tidyr::crossing(
    false_alarm_rate = seq(
      0, 1,
      length.out = 501
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hit_rate = pnorm(
      qnorm(false_alarm_rate) + d_prime_fit
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# 4. ORDER PANELS BY DISCRIMINABILITY
# Highest d' first
# ============================================================

model_order <- model_sdt_fits %>%
  arrange(desc(d_prime_fit)) %>%
  pull(model_name)

prompt_roc <- prompt_roc %>%
  mutate(
    model_name = factor(
      model_name,
      levels = model_order
    )
  )

roc_curves <- roc_curves %>%
  mutate(
    model_name = factor(
      model_name,
      levels = model_order
    )
  )

model_labels <- model_sdt_fits %>%

    # Allow long model names to wrap
    model_display = stringr::str_wrap(
      gsub("-", "- ", model_name),
      width = 25
    ),

    label = paste0(
      model_display,
      "\nd' = ",
      sprintf("%.2f", d_prime_fit)

# Need bar graph that shows difference between criterion and discriminability 
# --------------------------------------------------------
# Mean SDT estimates within each model and clarity level
# --------------------------------------------------------

clarity_model_means <- sdt_df %>%
  filter(
    prompt_family_short != "No Prompt",
    clarity_level %in% c("vague", "explicit", "explicit-fallback")
  ) %>%
  group_by(model_name, clarity_level) %>%
  summarise(
    d_prime = mean(d_prime, na.rm = TRUE),
    criterion = mean(criterion, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate changes relative to Vague, within each model
# --------------------------------------------------------

vague_reference <- clarity_model_means %>%
  filter(clarity_level == "vague") %>%
  select(
    model_name,
    vague_dprime = d_prime,
    vague_criterion = criterion
  )

clarity_changes <- clarity_model_means %>%
  filter(clarity_level != "vague") %>%
  inner_join(vague_reference, by = "model_name") %>%
  mutate(
    delta_dprime = d_prime - vague_dprime,
    delta_criterion = criterion - vague_criterion,
    clarity_short = factor(
      clarity_level,
      levels = c("explicit", "explicit-fallback"),
      labels = c("Explicit", "Explicit + Fallback")
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(delta_dprime, delta_criterion),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "change"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric = factor(
      metric,
      levels = c("delta_dprime", "delta_criterion"),
      labels = c("Discriminability (d')", "Response Criterion (c)")
    )
  )

# --------------------------------------------------------
# 95% confidence intervals across paired model differences
# --------------------------------------------------------

clarity_changes_summary <- clarity_changes %>%
  group_by(clarity_short, metric) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(change, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(change)),
    se = sd(change, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
    ci_low = mean - qt(0.975, n - 1) * se,
    ci_high = mean + qt(0.975, n - 1) * se,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --------------------------------------------------------
# Plot changes relative to Vague
# --------------------------------------------------------

# pooled np2
# --------------------------------------------------------
# Extract pooled partial eta-squared from Type II ANOVAs
# --------------------------------------------------------

extract_pooled_eta <- function(model, metric) {

  anova_df <- as.data.frame(car::Anova(model, type = 2))

  ss_error <- anova_df["Residuals", "Sum Sq"]

  tibble(
    term = rownames(anova_df),
    eta_p2 = anova_df[["Sum Sq"]] /
      (anova_df[["Sum Sq"]] + ss_error),
    metric = metric
  ) %>%
    filter(term %in% c("prompt_family_short", "clarity_level"))
}

sdt_pooled_effects <- bind_rows(
  extract_pooled_eta(m_dprime, "Discriminability (d')"),
  extract_pooled_eta(m_criterion, "Response Criterion (c)")
) %>%
  mutate(
    effect = factor(
      term,
      levels = c("prompt_family_short", "clarity_level"),
      labels = c("Prompt Family", "Prompt Clarity")
    ),
    metric = factor(
      metric,
      levels = c(
        "Discriminability (d')",
        "Response Criterion (c)"
      )
    )
  )

# --------------------------------------------------------
# Plot pooled effect sizes
# --------------------------------------------------------

p_sdt_pooled_effect_sizes <- ggplot(
  sdt_pooled_effects,
  aes(x = effect, y = eta_p2, fill = metric)
) +

  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7,
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +

  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", eta_p2)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 9
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Discriminability (d')" = "#85A9FA",
      "Response Criterion (c)" = "#F58F8B"
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 0.35),
    breaks = seq(0, 0.35, by = 0.05),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +

  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression("Partial " * eta[p]^2),
    fill = NULL
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_line(
      colour = "black",
      linewidth = 2,
      linetype = "solid"
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 26),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 34),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 26),
    legend.key.size = unit(1.3, "cm"),
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 26,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5
    )
  )

p_sdt_pooled_effect_sizes
```
